records.title: Transit Woes
records.primaryPattern: Discrete Event Simulation / Modular Arithmetic Headway Synchronization
records.factualScenarioSummary: Maintains running commute clock starting at s; adds walking interval d_i to reach stop i; computes bus departure wait using ceil((curr_time - s)/c_i)*c_i; adds bus travel time b_i; repeats for n bus routes and validates arrival before deadline t.

evidence.statementExcerpt: Every day Yraglac relies on his city’s local transit system to get to and from campus... Yraglac leaves his house every day at time s to make it to his first class which starts at time t. To get there, he takes n transit routes, one after the other... each bus only comes at an interval of every c_i... can you find out if he can make it to class on time?

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: industrial_simulation domain (Public Transit & Timetable Simulation). Multi-stage discrete event simulation tracking timeline clock with modular headway synchronization: wait = (c_i - (time % c_i)) % c_i. Verified multi-step logic.

records.title: Sim
records.primaryPattern: Interactive Text Buffer Simulation / Doubly Linked List / Deque Splice
records.factualScenarioSummary: Simulates interactive keystroke buffer processing character stream with Home ([), End (]), and Backspace (<). Tracks active insertion cursor position and performs O(1) text prepend/append/delete operations across up to 10^6 characters.

evidence.statementExcerpt: Each test case is a line containing the string that was written in the Text Editor Sim (Steven IMproved). The length of the string is at most 10^6... pressing "<" (Backspace) when cursor is at front does nothing. "[" (Home) moves cursor to front; "]" (End) moves cursor to back.

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: industrial_simulation domain (Text Editor Buffer Simulation). Large-scale text buffer simulation. Naive string splices cause quadratic O(N^2) TLE under 10^6 characters. Requires dynamic linked list or two deques to maintain O(1) cursor navigation and insertions.

records.title: Turtle Master
records.primaryPattern: 2D Grid Simulation / Finite State Machine / Collision Detection
records.factualScenarioSummary: Tracks autonomous robot turtle coordinates (r, c) and direction heading on an 8x8 grid. Executes command sequence (F=move forward, R=turn right 90 deg, L=turn left 90 deg, X=fire laser to melt ice castle). Detects grid boundary violations, rock collisions, invalid laser shots, and destination diamond arrival.

evidence.statementExcerpt: Robot Turtles is one of Theta’s favorite games... In the actual board game, an adult plays the role of the “turtle master,” which is the person that plays the role of a CPU to execute the program... F: moves forward... R: turns right 90 degrees... L: turns left 90 degrees... X: fires laser in direction facing to melt ice castle... Output Diamond! if entire program executes without error... Output Bug! if program error occurs.

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: industrial_simulation domain (Robotics & Autonomous Navigation). 2D finite state machine simulation tracking position (r, c), heading vector, grid mutations (melting ice), crash detection on rocks/borders, illegal laser firing, and termination state verification.

records.title: Disastrous Downtime
records.primaryPattern: Sliding Window / Discrete Concurrency Queue / Resource Sizing
records.factualScenarioSummary: Simulates incoming HTTP request stream over time. Maintains queue of active requests within 1000ms duration window. Tracks peak concurrent load across timeline and computes minimum server cluster capacity needed to handle peak load without packet loss.

evidence.statementExcerpt: You’re investigating what happened when one of your computer systems recently broke down... system was overloaded; it looks like it couldn’t handle the hailstorm of incoming requests... each server can work on at most k requests simultaneously... a request will take exactly 1000 milliseconds to process... minimum number of servers needed to prevent another system breakdown?

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: industrial_simulation domain (Cloud Infrastructure & Server Sizing). Sliding window concurrency queue / two-pointer event tracking over 10^5 events to find peak concurrent active requests and compute ceil(peak / k).

records.title: Elevator Trouble
records.primaryPattern: State Transition Graph / Breadth-First Search Simulation
records.factualScenarioSummary: Simulates discrete elevator motion across building of f floors. From current floor curr, valid transitions are curr + u (if <= f) and curr - d (if >= 1). Simulates BFS state exploration from start floor s to destination g to determine shortest sequence of button presses or verify unreachability.

evidence.statementExcerpt: You are on your way to your first job interview as a program tester, and you are already late. The interview is in a skyscraper and you are currently in floor s... elevator has only two buttons, marked “UP u” and “DOWN d”... find the shortest sequence of button presses you must press in order to get from s to g... or output “use the stairs”...

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: industrial_simulation domain (Building Automation & Elevator Dispatch). Unweighted shortest-path Breadth-First Search (BFS) over a 1D discrete state-space graph of 1,000,000 floor nodes with boundary enforcement.

records.title: The Dragon of Loowater
records.primaryPattern: Greedy Matching / Two Pointers / Cost Minimization
records.factualScenarioSummary: Simulates hiring knights to chop off dragon heads in Loowater kingdom. A knight of height h can chop a head of diameter d if h >= d, costing h gold coins. Sorts head diameters and knight heights in ascending order; greedily assigns the shortest sufficient knight to each head to minimize total gold expenditure or prove defense impossible.

evidence.statementExcerpt: Once upon a time, in the Kingdom of Loowater... Due to the lack of predators, the geese population was out of control... One day, a freak mutation occurred, and one of the geese spawned a multi-headed fire-breathing dragon... The knights’ union demands that for chopping off a head, a knight must be paid a wage equal to one gold coin for each centimetre of the knight’s height... minimize the expense...

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: greedy_optimization domain (Resource Allocation & Defense Optimization). Textbook greedy matching of two sorted arrays using two pointers.

records.title: Apartments
records.primaryPattern: Bipartite Greedy Matching / Two Pointers with Tolerance Window
secondaryPatterns: Housing Authority Applicant Matching & Resource Allocation
records.factualScenarioSummary: Simulates housing allocation matching n applicants with desired sizes a_i to m free apartments of size b_j. Applicant i accepts apartment j if |a_i - b_j| <= k. Sorts applicant demands and apartment sizes; uses two-pointer greedy progression to maximize total satisfied applicants.

evidence.statementExcerpt: There are n applicants and m free apartments. Your task is to distribute the apartments so that as many applicants as possible will get an apartment. Each applicant has a desired apartment size, and they will accept any apartment whose size is close enough to the desired size.

review.rationale: Phase 3.3.1 Statement Audited & Phase 3.3.1.2 Adjudicated Qualified Replacement: underrepresented_scenario domain (Housing Authority Applicant Matching & Resource Allocation). Standard two-pointer greedy matching on sorted arrays with a tolerance window k.
